summary: Contestants will draw two business-related topics, select one, and prepare a speech with no prior knowledge of the topic. They have up to ten minutes to prepare and must deliver a speech lasting three to five minutes, using only provided notecards. The speech is judged on delivery, organization, effectiveness, and adherence to event rules.
time_limits: No more than ten (10) minutes preparation
No less than three (3) and no more than five (5) minutes speech
SPEECH WILL BE STOPPED AT FIVE (5) MINUTES
submission_requirements: Notes can only be made on the notecards provided
No materials or previously prepared notes allowed into the preparation or presentation room
No personal electronic devices (smart watches, smart glasses, cell phone, etc.)
competencies: Demonstrate clear, professional, and effective oral communication when presenting ideas
Organize the speech using a clear introduction, body, and conclusion to create a coherent message
Use appropriate tempo, pitch, and vocal variety to enhance clarity and audience engagement
Use purposeful nonverbal gestures, posture, and eye contact to support confident delivery
Analyze the assigned topic quickly and develop key points supported by logical reasoning, examples, and relevant business insights
Adapt tone, language, and delivery to meet audience expectations
Use effective opening and closing statements to strengthen the overall message
Demonstrate professionalism, confidence, and ethical communication while presenting under pressure

rubric.description: If any question results in a NO, please assign a score of 0. If no to the question, please stop scoring and provide a brief reason for the disqualification:
Speaker maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
The speech content flows adequately, with a mostly clear structure and smooth transitions between points.

The speech comprehensively addresses the topic with a clear and focused approach. It includes relevant information that directly relates to the context given. The purpose of the speech (to decide, to impress, to inform, to persuade) is effectively achieved with clarity and impact.
The speech lasted no less than three (3) minutes and no more than five (5) minutes and the contestant did not use any materials other than those specified.

judging_notes: Finals may be part of the competition
The contestant will be given warnings via flash cards when there are two (2) minutes remaining and when there is (1) minute remaining during the speaking time
eligibility_notes: Any postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged event.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
